image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Triceratops skull mounted in a museum setting. The image focuses heavily on the head, showcasing the three horns (two long brow horns, one short nasal horn) and the large bony frill. The beak is visible at the front. The background shows museum walls and display stands. The body, limbs, and tail are not visible in this cropped shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic triceratops horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns and a smaller nasal horn. They project correctly relative to the skull structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rostral bone forming the beak is visible at the anterior of the skull, exhibiting the characteristic hooked, parrot-like shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up of the skull; the body and limbs are completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill is prominently visible extending backward from the skull. While the full width isn't seen due to the angle, the scale relative to the cranium is consistent with Triceratops anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated like Chasmosaurus). The texture is consistent with fossilized bone/mount material. Epoccipitals are somewhat visible along the margin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeletal mount/fossil display, so no skin or soft tissue is present to evaluate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in the frame.
The tail is not visible in the frame.

artifact_observations.location: Surface of the skull and frill
artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the 'bone' appears slightly uniform and plasticky, typical of a museum cast or restoration rather than raw fossil, but this is an attribute of the subject matter (a display model) rather than an AI generation error. However, slight smoothing artifacts are noticeable on the curved surfaces of the frill.

artifact_observations.location: Background display stands and wall lines
artifact_observations.reasoning: Minor perspective warping in the background vertical lines (museum pillars/stands), which is common in wide-angle photography but could also indicate slight AI spatial inconsistency. It is subtle.

To analyze the texture of the bone/surface for signs of AI 'smearing' or lack of fine detail typical in generated fossils.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the complex overhangs of the frill and horns, ensuring they don't melt into the background.
To check for clean boundaries between the dark skull and the lighter background, looking for haloing or fusion artifacts.

Also, verify if the texture looks like genuine stone/bone or if it has the 'waxy' sheen common in AI generations.
